Subject: Private offer — reseller margin & commitment tiering

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Stellar Health is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Procurement asked me to get a few clarifications before we move to a private offer:

1) We need to understand a recommended waterfall for reseller margin vs committed spend tiers (AWS private offer). Our reseller will want a clear % at each commit bracket.
2) Can we bundle inference SKU + support SKU into a single marketplace SKU or do you recommend two line items?
3) Any precedence on list price vs committed discount math (we'll pass some margin to the reseller).

Can your team sketch a proposal so procurement can review with our reseller (CloudFirst Partners)? Ideally a simple table with 3 tiers and suggested % splits.

Appreciate it — cc'd procurement.

Thanks,
Tim
VP, Platform Engineering
Stellar Health

Subject: Re: Private offer — reseller margin & commitment tiering

Tim — thanks, this is really clear. Looping in Vanessa (channel & marketplace) and Aditya (rev ops) to propose a concise waterfall and recommend SKU approach.

Quick thoughts up front:
- We generally recommend separate SKUs for compute (inference) and support/observability when customers want to trace costs, but we can ship a bundled SKU for procurement simplicity — caveat: bundling reduces flexibility for future rollups/discounts.
- Typical reseller margin bands we see: 10% at entry, 7% at mid commit (because vendor discount increases), 5% at highest commit — but that depends on whether you want the reseller to be selling primarily on price or service.

Vanessa/Aditya: can you prepare a table of three tiers, suggested list price, Redwood committed discount, and proposed reseller split? If feasible attach a quick worksheet the reseller can use.

Sofia
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private offer — reseller margin & commitment tiering

Tim / Sofia — attaching a compact worksheet that CloudFirst can use to model splits. I kept the fields intentionally simple: commit bracket, Redwood list price (monthly), Redwood discount to Stellar, reseller margin %, and net to Redwood.

Attachment: Reseller_RevShare_Template.xlsx (columns: Tier, Commit USD, List Price/unit, Redwood Discount %, Reseller Margin %, Net Unit to Redwood)

A few notes:
- If Stellar wants to preserve the reseller's commercial motivation, aim for a minimum 8–12% entry margin; if the reseller is providing managed onboarding/services we recommend the higher end (12%).
- Bundling: recommend a single bundled SKU only if you expect minimal SKU churn; otherwise two SKUs (inference + support) keeps ongoing negotiations simpler.
- Compliance/Procurement ask: AWS private offers can only be applied cleanly if the payment/commit is roped to the offer ID; we can provide the PO-level discount mapping but CloudFirst will still want their cut to show on the reseller invoice.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with CloudFirst to walk the worksheet.

—Vanessa
Head, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private offer — reseller margin & commitment tiering

Tim — following up with concrete numbers you can share with CloudFirst. I've modeled a conservative and an aggressive option. Attaching a quick private offer draft for your internal review.

Private Offer Draft (attached: Private_Offer_Draft.pdf) — highlights:
- Baseline list price (per-inference-unit): $0.045/token-equivalent
- Support/Observability add-on SKU: $1,200/month (optional line item)

Conservative waterfall (recommended for price-sensitive resellers):
- Tier A: $0–$100k/mo commit — Redwood customer discount: 20%; Reseller margin: 12%; Net to Redwood: (List * (1 - 0.20) * (1 - 0.12))
- Tier B: $100k–$400k/mo — Redwood discount: 28%; Reseller margin: 9%
- Tier C: >$400k/mo — Redwood discount: 35%; Reseller margin: 6%

Aggressive waterfall (higher commit incentives):
- Tier A: 18% discount / 14% reseller margin
- Tier B: 30% discount / 10% reseller margin
- Tier C: 40% discount / 6% reseller margin

Notes:
- If you bundle SKUs into a single marketplace SKU, our recommendation is to set the list price equal to combined list + 10% buffer to avoid early breakage when applying % discounts (we can calculate exacts).
- For AWS private offers we will provide the offer ID and the committed discount mapping tied to the HubSpot deal id. The reseller invoice can be issued separately; their margin is applied downstream and not reflected in the private offer payload.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.redwood.example/deals/PO-4692
AWS PO preview: https://na-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/privateoffers/offerId=abcd-1234

Happy to join the call and walk the math with CloudFirst and your procurement team.

—Aditya Rao
Director, Revenue Operations

2) Bundle inference + support into a single SKU for this first deployment to simplify internal chargebacks.
3) Request that Redwood populate the AWS private offer payload with the Tier B discount and send the offer ID so CloudFirst can prepare their invoice flow.

We will route the PO to your contracts address next week. Can you confirm you can: (a) publish a bundled SKU with the Tier B discount; (b) share the offer ID + HubSpot deal mapping once created; and (c) provide the reseller spreadsheet copy to CloudFirst?

If so we can lock the PO and get this into our August procurement run.

Thanks — I'll set up a 30-min sync if needed.
